header_sentences: See Burnt; and see Charcoal, and Inflame.

contexts.text: They were therefore left to their insane cupidities, which are here signified by the fire which is scattered over the city ().
Fire () = the punishment of cupidities.
Fire and flame () = evils and cupidities.
They first sank down into a fire which appeared, then into a fiery smoke like that of a furnace... While they sank through the fire, they lamented much. SE 1288.
There appears (in the Hell called Gehenna) as it were a kind of fieriness, like that which shows itself in the air from a great conflagration.

The burnt-offerings are called an offering made by fire for an odour of rest to Jehovah, by which is signified that which is from love and charity. Fire, and an offering made by fire, when predicated of the Lord, and of the worship of Him, = love. AC 2177:4.
Fire () = love. AC 3021:6.
A flaming fire () = the Celestial Spiritual.

As fire = love, it became a representative of the Lord, as is evident from the fire on the altar of burnt-offering, which was never to be put out (), representing the mercy of the Lord. Therefore, before Aaron entered into the propitiatory, he had to offer incense, taking the fire from the altar of burnt-offering (); and therefore also, in order to signify that the worship was accepted by the Lord, fire was sent down from heaven, and consumed the burnt-offerings (, and elsewhere.)

Fire also = the proper love and its cupidity, with which celestial love cannot agree; and therefore the two sons of Aaron were consumed by fire, because they burnt incense with strange fire (). Strange fire = all the love of self and of the world, and all the cupidity of these loves.

Moreover celestial love appears to the wicked as a burning and consuming fire; and therefore, in the Word, a consuming fire is predicated of the Lord; as the fire on Mount Sinai, which represented the love or mercy of the Lord, and was perceived before the people as a consuming fire... So does the Lord's love or mercy appear to those who are in the fire of the loves of self and of the world. AC 1861:15. AC 6365:2.

The sparkling coal according to the appearance of fire from his loins upward () = the Celestial of love; the brightness of fire round about from the loins downward as the bow in the cloud () = the Celestial Spiritual.
Fire () = the penalty of cupidities.
See Evil Spirit. AC 1528. AC 3195:2.
Under Cupidity, see this reference.
Fire = hatred. Illustrated. AC 1861:14, Illustrated.
In these passages fire = cupidities.
Hence it is evident what infernal fire is, and that it is nothing but hatred, revenge, and cruelty; or, what is the same, the love of self... Illustrated.
Fire = the infernal punishment of those who do not do these things; that is, who pass their time in the falsity of hatred. Illustrated.
(Thus) a torch of fire () = the most filthy evil, which, in the last times, will take possession of the Church.
The Gentiles derived their perpetual fires from the Ancient Church. AC 10177:10.
The (perpetual) fire on the altar represented the perpetual and eternal love, that is, mercy of the Lord. AC 4489:2.
The Holy Divine flowing into the profane with man, is of such efficacy, that it is like a devouring and consuming fire...
The love of self and its cupidities are signified by men being burned by the fire, and being scorched with great heat ().
Brimstone () = the Hell of the evils of the love of self; and fire = that of the falsities thence derived. AC 2446, Explained, Illustrated.
Fire = cupidities, and at the same time the Hells; and then the smoke from the fire = the falsity thence derived. Illustrated.
Under Chariot, see this reference. AC 2762:4.
He took in his hand fire and a knife () = the good of love and the truth of faith.
Behold the fire and the wood () = that love and justice are present.
As all good is of love, and love itself is celestial and spiritual fire, it is also compared to fire, and is also called fire. (See Red.)
Truth is of light; and good is the fire from which is the light. AC 5219.
Burnt with fire () = destroyed by concupiscences.
Under Sun, see this reference. AC 5079:end. AC 8812.
Light is not in fire, but proceeds from fire. The Divine good itself is compared to fire...
Spiritual fire and heat are love... All the vital fire and heat which are in the body are thence.
In the other life, when (such a man) is among the infernals, he is in the fire or heat of cupidities; but if he approaches Heaven, that fire and heat are turned into cold...

Fire and flame, in the spiritual sense, are good; consequently, heat is the affection of good. In the opposite sense, fire and flame are evil; consequently, heat is the affection of evil. Good, moreover, is actually spiritual fire, from which comes the spiritual heat which vivifies; and evil is the fire and consequent heat which consumes. That the good of love is spiritual fire, and that the affection of this good is spiritual heat, may be very evident to him who attends and reflects; for if he reflects whence come the vital fire and heat of man, he will find out that it is from love; for the moment love ceases, the man grows cold; and the more he is in love, the hotter he grows... But this spiritual fire or heat, which makes the life, becomes burning and consuming fire with the evil... AC 5071:2.

The eternal fire into which they were to depart () is not elementary fire; nor is it the torment of conscience; but it is the concupiscence of evil; for the concupiscences with man are spiritual fires which in the life of the body consume him, and in the other life torture him; by these infernal fires they torture each other in direful ways. Explained.
A flame of fire, and a stream of fire () represents the good of Divine love.

The sun is nothing but fire; and light is not in it, but proceeds from it... The sun represents the Lord; the fire therein His Divine love; the heat thence, the good which flows from that Love; and the light, the truth of faith. Therefore... fire = love. References.
Under Heat, see this reference.
See Bramble. AC 6833.

The reason a flame = the Divine love, is that love in its first origin is nothing but fire and flame from the Lord as a Sun. The fire or flame of this Sun is that which gives the being of life to every man; and is the vital fire itself... Hence when the Lord appeared in vision, He appeared as fire and flame. Illustrated.
The Divine good of the Lord's Divine love was here () seen as a flame of fire.
A flame of fire () = the Divine truth which is in the Word, which is from the Lord's Divine good.
That a flame of fire = the Divine truth proceeding from the Lord. Illustrated.
In order that the Divine good itself might be represented, it was commanded that the fire should be perpetual upon the altar.
That fire is a representative of the Divine love, was very well known to the ancients, (as is evident from the perpetual fires of the Gentiles).

That fire and flame, in the opposite sense, = filthy loves; as the loves of revenge, of cruelty, of hatred, of adultery; and, in general, the concupiscences which come from the loves of self and of the world. Illustrated.
Fire, and flame () = the cupidities of evil and falsity, which extinguish all the good and truth of the Church, and thus cause its vastation.

They who do not know that the vital fire in man is from a different origin than elementary fire, cannot possibly know otherwise than that by the fire of Hell is meant such fire as there is in the world; when yet, in the Word, no such fire is meant, but the fire which is of love, thus which is of the life of man, proceeding from the Lord as a Sun; and which fire, when it enters into those who are in things contrary, is turned into the fire of cupidities, which are... of revenge, hatred, cruelty, springing from the love of self and of the world. It is this fire which torments those who are in the Hells; for when the reins are given to their cupidities, the one rushes at the other, and they torment one another in direful and unspeakable ways...
See Divine Love.
The Lord a consuming fire. Explained. AC 8838.

Fire and brimstone () = the love of self and the cupidities thence derived; for the love of self and its cupidities are nothing but fire, not elementary fire, but fire from spiritual fire, which spiritual fire gives man his life. That loves are the vital fires is evident to him who reflects. It is these fires which are meant by the holy fires in the Heavens, and by the fires of Hell; elementary fire does not exist there.
That fire = the cupidity of evil. References.
[In Mars] they know how to make fluid fires, by which they get light during the evening and night.
A furnace of fire = the evils of cupidities; for the fire of cupidities is what is meant in the Word by the fire of Hell; moreover, loves are nothing but the fire of life...
Fire mingled with blood () = the evil of cupidities with falsified truths.
The fire walked on the earth () = the evils of cupidities... taking possession of the natural mind down to its lowest parts. AC 7577.
When (these evil Spirits) approach, there appears as it were a flying fire, which falls down near the face.
Roasted with fire () = the good of love... For fire = love. (See Roast.)
That fire, in the opposite sense, = the evil of the love of self and of the world, or of the cupidities which are of these loves. References.

The residue... ye shall burn with fire () = ... to undergo temptations. The reason temptations are signified by burning with fire, is that purifications are effected by means of fire; and also that when a man is in temptations, he is let into his cupidities, which are fires.
Under Column, see this reference.
Fire = the good of love. References. AC 8813:2.
Evil, then, is as fire; and falsities are as the lumen thence.
A refiner's fire () = temptation, by which there is purification.
Burning fire () = the things of love and charity.
The fire of Hell is nothing but the concupiscence which is of the love of self, which inflames and torments. References.

(The inhabitants of Jupiter) believe that after death they will perceive a fire, which will warm their faces. The origin of this idea is that the wiser of them know that the fire of the Spiritual World is love, and that this fire is the fire of life, and that the Angels have heat from this fire...
In the sun there is fire... but the fire itself of the sun does not pass to the Earth... but light in which there is heat from the fire of the sun.
The torment in Hell from falsity is compared to a worm; and the torment from evil there, is compared to fire. Illustrated.
It was therefore forbidden to kindle a fire on the Sabbath day (), because by a fire is signified everything that is of life; and by kindling a fire, that which is of life from the proprium.
Under Cook, see this reference.
Fire is in the sun, and light is from the sun; in the latter there is not fire, but heat... In the Sun there... there is Divine fire, which is the Divine good of the Divine love...
Divine good cannot be approached, because it is like the fire of the sun...
The faces (of those who call themselves saints) shine as it were from fire... but although their faces appear fiery, they are cold... (Thus) the fire from which they shine is like an ignis fatuus.
Because Jehovah descended upon it in fire () = the Divine there in celestial love. (For) the fire in which is Jehovah = Divine celestial love. That fire = love. References.
The fire which devours before Him () = the lust of evil; the flame which blazes after Him = the lust of the falsity thence derived.

The cupidities in man are fires which consume; for there exists in man the fire of life and the light of life; the fire of life is his love, and the light of life is his faith; the love of good, that is, love to the Lord and love towards the neighbour, make the fire of life with a good man and an Angel of Heaven... but the love of evil, that is, the love of self and the love of the world, make the fire of life with an evil man and a Spirit of Hell... But the love of evil is called in the Word the burning of fire, because it burns and consumes the things which are of the love of good and truth. References, Illustrated.

When fire shall go forth () = anger from the affection of evil; (for) fire = love; here, the love of evil and its affection; (and) when what a man loves is attacked, what is fiery bursts forth, and as it were burns. Hence anger is described by fire, and it is said to burn. Illustrated. AC 9147.
Anger is a fire bursting forth from the affection of evil; but zeal is a fire bursting forth from the affection of good. Illustrated.

The loves in man are the fires of his life; evil loves... are consuming fires, for they consume the goods and truths which are of the life itself; these fires constitute the life of man's will, and the light from these fires constitutes the life of his understanding. So long as the fires of evil are kept shut up in the will, the understanding is in light... but when these fires pour their light into the understanding, the former light is dissipated. (Continued. See Anger.)
The fire of wickedness and anger...
A fire of thorns () = the concupiscence of evil.
Fire and flame () = the love of self.
The fire with which the spoil and the city shall be burnt () = the evil of the love of self.
To be salted with fire () = the longing of good for truth.
There is a fiery principle in salt.
To kindle a fire with them seven years () = plenary destruction by the loves of self and of the world.
Fire out of (the bramble) () = the evil of concupiscence. AE 638:end.
Fire and brimstone () = the evils of the love of self and of the world. References.
So far as they are in the fires of the loves of self and of the world...
Strange fire in the censer () = doctrine from some other source than the Word; fire = the good of love...
That fire = the good of celestial love. References.
The fire with which the golden calf was burned () = the evil of the love of self and of the world.

The aspect of the glory of Jehovah was as a devouring fire... () = Divine truth in Heaven resplendent from the good of love, but inflicting injury and vastation on those who are in its external separated from its internal... Fire = love in both senses; here, the Divine love itself.

From love everyone has the heat and fire of his life. It is evident that without vital heat and fire there is no life... Love is as a fire or flame in man, and is also the vital fire or flame; and faith is as the light from this fire or flame...

With those who are in heavenly love, the Divine fire or love is continually creating and renovating the interiors of the will, and illuminating the interiors of the understanding; but with those who are in infernal love, the Divine fire or love is continually inflicting injury and vastation. The reason is that with the latter the Divine love falls into opposite things, by which it is destroyed; for it is turned into the fire or love of self and of the world, thus into contempt for others, into enmities... hatred, revenge, and fierceness. Hence it is that the fire of Jehovah appeared before their eyes as a devouring or consuming one... Illustrated.
Devouring fire = vastation. Illustrated.
In these passages a devouring fire = the fire of the cupidities which are from the loves of self and of the world, because this is the fire which consumes man, and which vastates the Church.

To put strange fire in their censers = to institute worship from some other love than heavenly love. That such fire = the love of self and of the world, and all the cupidity thence derived. References. AE 504:21.
Fire () = the infernal love of evil.
The fire of the altar = the good of Divine love. References. Therefore... strange fire = love not Divine.
The fire of the altar (which was to be constantly burning) = the Divine good of the Lord's Divine love.
A great mountain burning with fire () = the love of self.
As the internal man is opened to the Lord... so it is in the fire of Heaven... The fire of Heaven is the Divine love proceeding from the Lord; from this is kindled the will of good.
The fire of the life of the world extinguishes the fire of the life of Heaven.
Fire () = concupiscence, which, being from evil, destroys.
To make them a flaming lire () = I receptions of Divine good or of Divine love.
To baptize with fire () = to regenerate from the Divine good of the Divine love. DLord 51. TCR 144:end. TCR 684. TCR 686. AE 374:14. AE 475:20. AE 504:7.
Under Urim, see this reference.
The fire of the altar represented the Divine love, thus love from the Lord; but strange fire, love from Hell: the annihilation of worship is signified by offering incense with this fire.
Thou shalt burn with fire outside the camp () = that these things are to be committed to Hell and consumed by the evils of the love of self. Explained.
There are two fires of life with man; one is the love of self, and the other is love to God...
Thou shalt burn the rest with fire () = their dissipation... by the loves which are proper to man, thus by the evils of these loves.
The food of fire () = the appropriation of the evils or cupidities of the love of self and of the world.
To kindle a fire (on the Sabbath day) = to do what is good from our Own loves. AC 10732.
Hence come intestine hatreds, fiercenesses, and cruelties, which are what are signified by infernal fires.

He burnt (the calf) with fire () = entirely from the loves of self and of the world, which are condemned to Hell. Fire = celestial love, which is love to the Lord and love towards the neighbour; and in the opposite sense, infernal love, which is the love of self and the love of the world. References. Hence to be burnt with fire = to be entirely filled with the loves of self and of the world, thus to be condemned to Hell... From this it is evident what is signified by the infernal fire mentioned in the Word passim.
I cast it into the fire () = into the loves of self and of the world...

Heavenly fire is love to the Lord and love towards the neighbour; and infernal fire is the love of self and the love of the world, and thus the concupiscence of all the evils which spring from these loves. HH 134. HH 568.
Divine love is the fieriness appearing around the Lord in that Sun.
Love is like the fire of the sun.
This is because the good of love corresponds to fire; and therefore fire, in the spiritual sense, is love; and the good of faith corresponds to light.
The fieriness of the world corresponds to the love of self...
Their infernal fire is the cupidity of glory and of name, by which the one is carried against the other...
The delights of the love of self and of the world are then turned into painful and direful things, because into such things as are called infernal fire... DP 83:3.
What infernal fire is. General article.
Infernal fire or love comes forth from the same origin as heavenly fire or love; namely, from the Sun of Heaven, but it is made infernal by those who receive it. Explained.
Infernal fire, therefore, is the cupidity and delight which spring from these two loves.
These are the things which are meant by fire in the Word. Enumerated, Illustrated.
In these and many other places, by fire is meant the cupidity which is of the love of self and of the world; and by the smoke thence is meant the cupidity of evil.

Therefore, when the Hells are opened, there is an appearance as of fire with smoke, such as is seen in conflagrations; a dense fieriness from the Hells where the love of self reigns; and a flaminess from those where the love of the world reigns. But when they are closed, this fieriness is not seen... Yet it still rages within...
But those who are in the Hells are not in fire, but the fire is an appearance... for love corresponds to fire.
This fire or infernal heat is turned into intense cold when heat from Heaven flows in...
As infernal fire means every cupidity... by the same fire is meant torment. Described. HH 574:end. Described.
Fire corresponds to hatred and revenge.
Those who were in the insane love of exercising command over all, appeared fiery.
The sun is a fiery ocean.
The Sun (of Heaven) appears fiery, because love and fire correspond to each other... Divine love is also felt as fire by spiritual beings. Hence, where fire is mentioned in the Word, it = love...
A sun which is pure fire... fire is dead, and the solar fire is death itself...

The acme of spiritual heat is spiritual fire, which is the Divine love and the Divine wisdom in their first correspondence. Hence it is that that Sun appears fiery, and also that it is fiery to the Angels, but not to men. The fire which is fire to men is not spiritual, but natural; and the difference between the two fires is like that between living and dead. DLW 97.
This spiritual fire... becomes spiritual heat and light...
The sun means the Lord as to the Divine love and Divine wisdom together; fire means Him as to Divine love: and light, as to Divine wisdom.
That the sun of the natural world is pure fire, and thence dead... DP 3:2. AR 468.

The angelic idea concerning the fire of the (natural) sun, and the fire of the (spiritual) Sun, is that the Divine life is internally in the fire of the (spiritual) Sun, but externally in the fire of the (natural) sun.
Thus the fire of the sun becomes heat. (See Atmosphere here, and at DLW 175.)
Dusky fieriness is the opposite to red.
See Concupiscence.
The evil perform uses from a stronger fire...
Gold tried in the fire () = the good of celestial love. ( = genuine good. AE 242.)
No one in Hell is in flame, but the flame is the appearance of the love of falsity; and the fire, of the love of evil.
The Angel filled the censer with the fire of the altar () = spiritual love in which is celestial love. AE 496.

The fire of the altar of burnt-offering = Divine celestial love; (for) fire, in the highest sense, = the Divine love. Spiritual love derives its essence from celestial love... This was represented by their taking fire for the censers solely from the altar of burnt-offering... (And) the fire on it was to burn continually... because it = the Lord's Divine love, and hence love to the Lord. AE 496:2. AE 496:4.
Hail and fire () = falsity from infernal love. Illustrated. AE 503, Illustrated.
Every love, when excited, there appears at a distance as fire...
Fiery breastplates () = their argumentations imaginary and visionary from infernal love.
Out of their mouths issued fire... () = that in their thoughts and discourses, viewed interiorly, there is nothing else, and from them proceeds nothing else, than the love of self and of the world...
Fire = infernal love; and brimstone, the concupiscences flowing from this love through the conceit of Own intelligence. Illustrated.
The fire of his loins () = celestial love. ( = His Divine love. AR 830:3.)
His feet as pillars of fire () = the Lord's Divine Natural as to Divine love, which sustains all things.
The reason fire = love, is that spiritual fire is nothing else...
That fire = Divine love. Illustrated.
Fire shall proceed out of their mouth () = infernal love (which is really not from the two witnesses, but from those who are in infernal love). Illustrated. AE 642.
Fire and smoke then came out of the Word.
He maketh fire to come down from heaven... () = proofs that their falsities are the truths of Heaven. Explained, Illustrated. AE 825.
Moreover, fire = celestial love, and thence zeal for truth; and in the opposite sense, infernal love, and thence zeal for falsity.
Shall be tormented with fire and brimstone... () = the love of self and the love of the world and the cupidities therefrom... AE 888.
Having Power over fire () = ... that the Angels guard the Divine love in themselves. AE 916.
There appeared as it were fire from Heaven which consumed them; but the fire from Heaven was an appearance of their anger from hatred... AR 714:end.
Mingled with fire () = religion and worship, but no good of life... Fire, here, = the love of evil, and from it evil of life. ( = the good of love. AE 931.)
The fire of the altar of burnt-offering = celestial love; and the fire of the altar of incense, spiritual love. References.
Hatred against the Lord, and against all things of Heaven and the Church, is meant by the fire in Hell.
She shall be utterly burnt with fire () = that they will be hatreds against the Lord, and against His Heaven and Church.
Infernal fire is hatred, because the love of self hates...
To be burned with fire is the penalty of the profanation of what is holy.
The lake of fire burning with brimstone () = the Hell where are they who are in the loves of this falsity, and at the same time in the cupidities of evil. AR 864. AR 893.
Fire came down from God out of Heaven and consumed them () = that they perished by the concupiscences of infernal love. Explained.
The fire of the (spiritual) Sun is in its essence the Lord's Divine love, thus the good of love.
The fire of the angelic Sun, which is pure love, is the cause (of man's vital heat).

There appeared as it were a lake of fire and brimstone. I asked the Angel why the Hells so appear. He replied, They appear like lakes from falsifications of truth... and there appears as it were fire around and in them from the love of evil; and as it were brimstone, from the love of falsity.
There again appeared those two lightnings... and the left hand lightning derived its shining whiteness from the red-shining fire of that on the right... because fieriness in Heaven is good...
In the will, love is as fire; and in the understanding as flame.

The fire of the (natural) sun comes from the Sun of Heaven, which is not fire, but the Divine love proximately proceeding from God... (For) love in its essence is spiritual fire; hence fire, in the Word, = love... (Thus) the fire of the natural sun has come forth from no other source than the fire of the spiritual Sun, which is Divine love. ISB 6. TCR 35:12.
Infernal fire is nothing but love which is opposite to heavenly love.
The sun of nature... is pure fire... and the nature of its heat is like the heat from elementary fire... (Thus) the sun... is mere fire: and is, moreover, fire in its purity itself.
Love is alive, and the appearance of its fire is life; but... elementary fire, regarded in itself, is relatively dead...

Divine love forms life as fire forms light. There are two things in fire; that of burning, and that of shining; from its burning property proceeds heat, and from its shining property light. So there are two things in love; one to which the burning property of fire corresponds, which is something that most interiorly affects the will; and the other to which the shining property of fire corresponds, which is something that most interiorly affects the understanding; and hence man has love and intelligence.

This may be illustrated by the (natural) sun, which is pure fire; for heat proceeds from its fieriness, and light from the brightness of its fieriness; and thus both, in their origin, are one. TCR 75:2. TCR 76:2. TCR 77:3.

I saw a great smoke, and fire occasionally bursting out of it... Smoke seen in the Hells arises from falsities confirmed by reasonings; and fire is anger blazing up against those who contradict. (Continued. See Flame.)
They were so enraged that smoke and fire came out of their nostrils.
(From such a faith it follows) that fire is life from God.
Like fire in wood under the ash. Infernal fire is nothing else...
Hatred shows like dusky fires, and revenge like bright fires.
Evil is like fire and it consumes faith like stubble.
The sun of this world consists of created substances, the activity of which produces fire.
This is the fire by which the world will perish, if it does not repent. Explained.
Punishment by fire, which as it were burns their lascivious members. SE 1980.
That (David) made them pass through the fire... is denied; for... the internals are intensely horrified at the phantasy of fire.
On the appearances to Spirits as of little fires.
Under Gehenna, see this reference. SE 3468.
They can become both fire and ice...
They are nocturnal fiery lights...
They are then surrounded with sulphur and with fire therefrom.
Heavenly and infernal fire. Explained.
Appearance as of an ocean of fire.
See Charles XII.
Evil Italians retain a fire within themselves...
Around them appears a fieriness...
There sometimes appears a flaming fieriness wandering about them in the streets where they are walking, but it is a consuming fire...
On the cruelty of some by means of fire and tow.
On a rain of fire and brimstone.
Fiery, when said of the Lord, = that which is from the Divine love.
Fire = His Divine good. AE 183:12.
A flaming fire = the Divine love and the Divine good thence. ( = the good of love. AE 155:2.) ( = the good of love and the truth thence. AE 419:11.)
Fire = the love of self. AE 455:16. AE 730:14.
Fire = infernal loves.
Fire = the good of love.
Love, there, appears as fire.
Fire = love, in both senses. AE 539:14. AE 825. AE 888.
The fire of the altar = celestial good. ( = Divine celestial love. AE 324:6.) ( = the Divine good of His Divine love. AE 391:8.)
A stream of fire going forth () = the Divine good of love.
Into the fire () = into the evils which are from the love of self.
The fire in Hell is like a coal fire.
Fire = the love of evil. AE 638:17.
A fire of coal = the evil of our Own love.
Fire = the love of self and the love of the AE 405:42. AE 540:6. AE 811:8.
Torch of fire () = the hideous love of self.
Infernal love in man is such a fire...
The Word is said to be as a fire (), because fire = the good of love.
Fire and hail () = the delights of the loves of the natural man.
Fire = the love of truth.
The rain of hail and fire. Explained.
On the signification of fire. General article.

Fire, in the Word, = the good of celestial love; and flame, the good of spiritual love: and in the opposite sense, fire = evil originating in the love of self; and flame, evil originating in the love of the world. Illustrated.
Fire = the Lord's Divine love. Illustrated. AE 595:4. AE 597.

Where fire is said of the evil and of the Hells, it = the love of self and of the world, and every evil affection and cupidity thence derived which torments the wicked after death in the Hells. The reason fire = these opposite things, is that when the Divine love descends from Heaven, and falls into the Societies where the evil are, it is turned into love contrary to the Divine love, and thus into various ardours of cupidities and concupiscences... and as evils carry their own penalties with them, it is turned into torments... AE 504:16, Illustrated. AE 504:20.
The Divine influx with the good appears in the Heavens as a fire vivifying, recreating, and conjoining; but with the evil below, as a fire consuming and vastating. AE 504:19, Illustrated.
As fire = the love of self... fire = every evil; as enmity, hatred, revenge... Consequently, fire also = the destruction of man as to spiritual life, and thus damnation and Hell. Illustrated.
to go through the fire and not be burnt () = that evils shall not hurt.
A great mountain burning with fire () = the love of self and Own intelligence thence.
To prove by fire () = by the affection of love; for if truth does not agree with this, it is not genuine.
Fire () = the good of the Word adulterated.
Fire = evils. AE 540:9. AE 543:10.
They are said to kindle a fire () when they approve and excite from the love of evil.
Fire and brimstone = evils of falsity and falsities of evil. AE 578:7. AE 578:8, Illustrated.
Fire = His presence by Divine good, which is called the good of faith, being last in order. Illustrated.
The fire kindled in the lamps = spiritual love, which is love towards the neighbour.
Fire = natural love.
